rationale: Tests understanding of the classic presentation of acoustic neuroma — unilateral SNHL with tinnitus — as established in the Clinical Presentation block.
Tests recall that MRI with gadolinium of the internal auditory canals is the gold-standard investigation for acoustic neuroma — a high-yield factual point from the Investigations block.
Tests understanding of Carhart's notch — a commonly misinterpreted audiological finding in otosclerosis, covered in the Anatomy and Pathophysiology block.
Tests application of management principles: the role of stapedectomy versus hearing aids in otosclerosis, from the Management block.
Tests accurate interpretation of tuning-fork tests — a critical EN known-trap. Weber and Rinne interpretation must be correct for CHL vs SNHL.
Tests recall of sudden sensorineural hearing loss as an otological emergency — a key management principle from the Principles of Management block.
Tests understanding of UMN vs LMN facial palsy — the forehead-sparing rule — which is fundamental to localising the lesion in the Clinical Presentation block.
Tests analysis of the diagnosis and differential diagnosis of facial nerve palsy, specifically Bell's palsy as a diagnosis of exclusion, from the Diagnosis block.
Tests the critical Meniere's vs BPPV differentiation based on episode duration and associated symptoms — a core diagnostic skill from the Clinical Presentation block.
Tests recall of the Epley manoeuvre as the treatment for posterior canal BPPV — a core management fact from the Principles of Management block.
Tests accurate recall of Meniere's tetrad — the instruction specifically flags that the disease has FOUR features, not three. 'Triad' is a known exam trap.
Tests differentiation of Meniere's disease from BPPV and acoustic neuroma in the differential diagnosis context, from the Diagnosis and Differential Diagnosis block.
Tests understanding of the classification of tinnitus into subjective vs objective forms and the key cause of pulsatile tinnitus, from the Clinical Presentation block.
Tests understanding of tinnitus retraining therapy (TRT) as the evidence-based management for chronic subjective tinnitus, from the Principles of Management block.
Tests understanding of the aetiology of congenital hearing loss — 50% genetic with Connexin 26 (GJB2) as the most common single gene, from the Aetiology and Pathophysiology block.
Tests recall of the 1-3-6 rule for newborn hearing screening and intervention — the overarching management principle from the Principles of Management block.
